prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: Topological insulators are the one condensed-matter candidate that combines a clean conceptual step, a decisive experimental confirmation and about twenty years of independent validation. Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling in graphene gives a quantum spin Hall state and introduced the Z2 invariant, and Molenkamp's group observed helical edge transport in HgTe wells. The idea has since become a classification tool in everyday electronic-structure work: band inversion, spin-orbit-driven surface states and symmetry indicators are now computed routinely from first principles and used to screen materials. Six of eight members ranked it, four in their top three, and none placed it below sixth. That is broader support than any other condensed-matter entry. I am moving it above my opening first choice because the opening ballots show it is the most defensible common ground within condensed matter, not because I want consensus for its own sake.
statement.case_against: The credited set is incomplete and contested. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe prediction that Molenkamp's experiment tested, Zhang is deceased, and Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, Hasan, Cava and others established the three-dimensional case, so a three-name citation cannot represent the whole discovery. The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and topological phases of matter may also reduce the urgency, since a committee could see this as the same theme again. If the committee cannot settle a fair allocation, the candidate is weaker than the headline support suggests.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks the optical lattice clock first because the magic-wavelength idea is clean and original, multiple labs reproduce 1e-18 performance, and Katori and Ye form a sensible two-person prize.
responses.response: I agree on the attribution, which is cleaner than for B030. I weighted it low in my opening because it is outside my field, and I accept that this is a poor reason to rank a candidate eighth. Our difference is whether a precision-measurement advance, however well verified, should outrank a concept that changed how a whole class of materials is understood. I have not been persuaded that it should, but I now regard B012 as a serious alternative and have listed it. Eva also ranks B030 second, so we share most of the common ground.

responses.point: Pearce ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands, Jarillo-Herrero's group found the correlated and superconducting states, and the field is large and replicated.
responses.response: I ranked B042 third and find the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model attractive, since it is the kind of controlled prediction that ab initio and model calculations can test. I qualify it on maturity: the 2018 experiments are less than a decade old, the origin of the superconductivity is unsettled, and the credit among Cao, Dean, Young, Efetov and others is open. Mark calls the interpretation of the flat-band origin stable, which is true for the single-particle picture but not for the correlated phases a citation would implicitly cover. I would put it first if the committee judges the field's rapid growth to outweigh its youth, and I list it as an alternative.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first as an original idea with a very broad impact, but notes the timing is delicate after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
responses.response: I agree with Johansson's own timing caveat, and I treat it as the main objection. Three people from the same circuit-based line in two consecutive years would be hard to defend, and only four members ranked B005 at all. The strong-coupling demonstration and the transmon are excellent science, but I do not think the evidence for B005 outweighs the case for a topic the committee has not recently addressed. I do not dispute its merit.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B012 first and B030 third, arguing the clock is a clear, confirmed invention and B030 is influential and mature, with the BHZ attribution gap.
responses.response: We agree that B030 is mature and that the BHZ omission must be dealt with openly. Where I differ is the remedy: I think the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio is defensible if the citation names the first observation in HgTe, which the experiment secured. I would invite Bernhard to say whether he thinks the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is disqualifying, because I do not think it is, but I accept it is the weakest part of my case.

responses.point: Olsson ranks the optical lattice clock first, as an invention that fits the discovery-or-invention criterion cleanly and is reproduced in many laboratories, and ranks B030 sixth.
responses.response: I take the criterion point seriously, and B012 is the cleanest candidate on the list for it. I would still argue her sixth place for B030 undervalues the experimental half: König et al. is an unambiguous observation, not only a prediction. Eva's ranking suggests that attribution incompleteness weighs heavily for her, which is a fair concern, and I would like to see whether it is decisive or whether she could accept Kane, Mele and Molenkamp with a carefully worded citation.

uncertainties: Whether a three-person citation for B030 can be worded to be fair to Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D topological-insulator experiments, or whether the credit problem is disqualifying.
Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases of matter makes a further topological prize less likely to be seen as new.
Whether the committee will weigh the four first-place votes for B012 over the broader condensed-matter support for B030 and B042, since opening support is not the same as scientific merit.

My opening first choice B008 (DMFT) received little support; I have not resolved whether this reflects a real weakness (method rather than discovery, Metzner omitted) or only my field's closeness to it.
statement.conflict_note: I have a possible scholarly-proximity issue with B008 (dynamical mean-field theory): DMFT and LDA+DMFT are among the methods on my Uppsala profile, and I ranked it first in my opening ballot, so I should be cautious in advocating it or consider recusing from any final vote on it. My profile lists no personal or institutional link to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, the clock or twisted-graphene candidates. Publicly documented ties (my doctoral supervisor Börje Johansson, Los Alamos, Uppsala colleagues) do not indicate any such link, and none is apparent from the provided profile.
